answer: New identities moor at a public jetty: each posts a 6 POA bond and completes one useful job, re-performed by independent verifiers. The verifier count is the square of the identities already funded from the same wallet — the 1st fake faces 1 verifier, the 2nd faces 4, the 10th faces 100. Each verifier is paid 1 POA from the bond, so the 1st fake costs 7 POA, the 10th 106 POA, 385 POA across ten fakes. A mismatch slashes the whole bond and nails the identity to the public timber board, where later verifiers read the ripple of its fraud before trusting a new mooring.
